# Kane CLI Documentation

> Kane CLI by TestMu AI (formerly LambdaTest) - an AI-powered command-line tool that runs browser and native mobile end-to-end (E2E) tests in natural language, from your terminal, IDE, or CI pipeline.

Each link below points to the plain-Markdown copy at `/docs/<slug>.md`.

Sitemap: https://www.testmuai.com/sitemap.xml

## Agent skill

- [Kane CLI Agent Skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LambdaTest/kane-cli/main/skill-installer/skills/SKILL.md): Instructions that teach an AI coding agent how to use kane-cli - when to invoke it, how to build the command, how to read the NDJSON output, and how to diagnose a failed run.
- [Kane CLI AGENTS.md for coding agents](https://www.testmuai.com/kane-cli-agent/AGENTS.md): The full instruction file for agents that read AGENTS.md, such as Cursor and GitHub Copilot.

## Docs

- [Kane CLI: AI Test Automation Overview](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-introduction.md): Kane CLI is an AI-powered command-line tool that runs browser and native mobile app tests in plain English: from your terminal, IDE, or CI pipeline.
- [How to Install Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-installation.md): Install Kane CLI using npm or Homebrew. Supports macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Linux (x64 and arm64), and Windows (x64).
- [How to Run Your First Kane CLI Test](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-quickstart.md): Authenticate Kane CLI and run your first browser automation test in under 5 minutes.
- [How to Authenticate Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-authentication.md): Authenticate Kane CLI with OAuth or basic auth, manage multiple profiles, and securely store credentials.
- [Kane CLI Modes: TUI, Headless & Agent](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-modes.md): Kane CLI has three modes: Interactive TUI for development, Headless CLI for scripts and CI/CD, and Agent Mode for AI coding agent integrations.
- [How to Write Kane CLI Objectives](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-writing-objectives.md): Learn the three objective patterns: actions, assertions, and extractions: and how to write natural language objectives that produce reliable test results.
- [How to Make API Calls with Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-api-calls.md): Have the Kane CLI agent make HTTP API calls directly inside an objective to seed data, hit a backend, then assert on or reuse the response.
- [How to Set Browser State in Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-browser-state.md): Set cookies, localStorage, and the clipboard directly from a Kane CLI objective to seed state before a flow or test copy and paste behavior.
- [How to Use Variables in Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-variables-and-context.md): Use variables to parameterize objectives with secrets and reusable values. Use context files to give the agent project-specific knowledge.
- [How to Configure Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-configuration.md): Configure Kane CLI settings including window size, Chrome profiles, Test Manager project and folder, run mode, and code export.
- [How to Upload Kane CLI Tests to Test Manager](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-tms-integration.md): Kane CLI uploads every session to TestMu AI Test Manager as a test case. Learn the upload pipeline, project and folder selection, code export, and share links.
- [How to Write Kane CLI Tests in Markdown](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-testmd.md): Write browser tests as Markdown that replay from cache after the first run: no LLM cost, faster runs. Commit to git, share recordings, and run in CI.
- [Composing Tests (@import)](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-testmd-composition.md): Split a test.md into reusable helper files with @import: syntax, path resolution, optional imports, what propagates, variables across imports, helper outputs and sharing helpers across projects.
- [Running test.md Files](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-testmd-running.md): Run and replay test.md files with kane-cli testmd: the full flag reference, how a run works, replay versus author, the cascade rule, lock conflicts, output directory, exit codes and the testmd list, status, delete, export and sync commands.
- [Batch Runs (testrun)](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-testrun.md): Run many authored _test.md files as one execution with kane-cli testrun run: tag and regex selection, parallel workers, preflight, dry runs, exit codes and a single sealed evidence pack.
- [Remote Runs on the Cloud Grid](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-remote-execution.md): Dispatch a suite of _test.md files to HyperExecute with kane-cli testrun run --remote: grid browsers for web suites, grid emulators and simulators, and real Android and iOS devices, from any machine.
- [How to Test Mobile Apps with Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-mobile.md): Run Kane CLI tests on mobile virtual devices, locally on macOS Apple Silicon or on the cloud grid from any machine. Set up the iOS Simulator or the Android Emulator and drive a native app.
- [How to Test on Real Android and iOS Devices with Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-mobile-real-device.md): Run Kane CLI native app tests on real Android and iOS devices in the TestMu AI cloud from any machine. Pick a device, pass an .apk, .aab, or .ipa build, and run single tests or suites.
- [Kane CLI Use Cases by Category](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-use-cases.md): Browse Kane CLI use cases by category, from API testing to everything you can drive with a single natural-language command.
- [API Testing Use Cases](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/api-testing-with-kane-cli.md): API testing use cases for Kane CLI, from smoke tests and auth-token chaining to schema validation, SLA gates, and multi-step API transactions, each with the exact steps to follow.
- [How to Use Kane CLI with AI Coding Agents](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-with-ai-coding-agents.md): See how Kane CLI gives AI coding agents a real browser, with walkthroughs for Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and Kiro, plus patterns that work in any agent.
- [How to Generate Test Cases with Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-generate.md): Turn a plain-language description of what to test into structured scenarios and test cases with kane-cli generate, then save them as runnable _test.md files.
- [How to Use the Kane CLI Generate Flow](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-generate-workflow.md): Walk the kane-cli generate loop end to end: generate, refine in plain language, save functional cases as _test.md files, and run them with testmd.
- [The Kane CLI Assurance Lifecycle](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-assurance.md): Go from requirements to designed, runnable tests with the kane-cli assurance commands: every test linked to what it verifies, coverage from evidence.
- [How to Build the Kane CLI Context Graph](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-assurance-context.md): Snapshot requirement documents into a local, content-addressed store and extract use-cases with an AI agent using kane-cli context.
- [Requirement Sources](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-assurance-sources.md): Every source type kane-cli can ingest as a requirement: text, PDF, Word documents, images, and remote sources by URL including Jira issues, Confluence pages, Linear issues and documents, and public web pages.
- [How to Design Kane CLI Tests from Use-Cases](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-assurance-design.md): Turn one use-case into acceptance criteria, scenarios, and one runnable test per scenario with kane-cli design tests: reviewed, cited, and linked.
- [How to Measure Kane CLI Test Coverage](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-assurance-coverage.md): Measure Kane CLI coverage on two axes with kane-cli cover: what a sealed evidence pack proved and what the design still owes, plus a gaps worklist.
- [How to Maintain a Kane CLI Test Suite](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-assurance-maintain.md): Keep tests aligned with changing requirements: kane-cli maintain reconcile triages each changed source into an ADD/MODIFY/ARCHIVE plan you approve.
- [Sharing the Context Graph with Your Team](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-assurance-sharing.md): Share a .context store with your team through a GitHub repository, an S3-compatible bucket or a shared folder: kane-cli context push, pull, sync, clone, and the decisions when two people change the same thing.
- [How to Run Kane CLI Assurance in CI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-assurance-automation.md): The headless contract for kane-cli assurance: the --mode ask policy, exit codes, NDJSON event streams, and the pause-answer-resume loop.
- [Kane CLI Evidence Packs Explained](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-evidence.md): Every kane-cli run seals an evidence pack: a portable .evidence file with the test definition, per-step screenshots, console and network logs, and failures.
- [Kane CLI Evidence Pack Structure](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-evidence-pack-structure.md): What is inside a kane-cli .evidence pack and what each part is for, from the run.yaml manifest anchor to per-step screenshots, logs, and failure records.
- [How to View Kane CLI Evidence Packs](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-evidence-viewing.md): Open a kane-cli evidence pack in the hosted viewer with kane-cli evidence serve, a localhost-only server that uploads nothing.
- [How to Validate Kane CLI Evidence Packs](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-evidence-validate.md): Check a kane-cli evidence pack's integrity and completeness with kane-cli evidence validate, including the L0 and L1 profiles and CI-friendly exit codes.
- [How to Merge Kane CLI Evidence Packs](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-evidence-merge.md): Combine several kane-cli evidence packs into a single sealed pack with kane-cli evidence merge, including the strict default policy and collision handling.
- [How to Debug a Failed Kane CLI Run](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-evidence-debugging.md): Use a kane-cli evidence pack to find why a run failed: the failed step, its console and network logs, the annotated screenshot, and the failed-vs-broken split.
- [The Kane CLI .evidence Format](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-evidence-format.md): The open, framework-agnostic .evidence format behind kane-cli packs: the L0 and L1 profiles, what sealing guarantees, and the Apache-2.0 evidence-cli tooling.
- [How to Use Checkpoints in Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-checkpoints.md): Checkpoints are verification points KaneAI evaluates during test execution: assert conditions, branch on results, or extract values for later use.
- [How to Assert Visuals in Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-checkpoint-visual.md): Verify what is visible on the screen by analyzing the current screenshot. Request visual assertions explicitly with --assertion-mode visual.
- [How to Assert DOM Values in Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-checkpoint-textual.md): Extract data from the DOM (element states, attributes, and computed styles) and assert on values that may not be visible in a screenshot.
- [How to Assert the URL in Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-checkpoint-url.md): Check values in the browser address bar: current URL path, query parameters, fragments, and redirect targets.
- [How to Assert the Page Title in Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-checkpoint-title.md): Verify the browser tab document.title, useful for confirming navigation reached the expected page.
- [How to Assert DevTools Data in Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-checkpoint-devtools.md): Verify data that is not visible on the page: HTTP network traffic, console output, performance metrics, cookies, localStorage, and clipboard.
- [How to Assert Network Traffic in Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-checkpoint-devtools-network.md): Verify HTTP traffic (API responses, status codes, headers, response bodies, and request timing) captured by KaneAI in the background.
- [How to Assert Console Logs in Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-checkpoint-devtools-console.md): Verify browser console output: errors, warnings, log messages, and JavaScript exceptions captured during test execution.
- [How to Assert Performance in Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-checkpoint-devtools-performance.md): Verify Core Web Vitals and other performance metrics (LCP, CLS, INP, FCP, TTFB) captured during test execution.
- [How to Assert Cookies in Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-checkpoint-devtools-cookies.md): Verify browser cookies (names, values, and flags such as httpOnly, secure, and sameSite) set during test execution.
- [How to Assert localStorage in Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-checkpoint-devtools-localstorage.md): Verify key-value pairs stored in the browser localStorage during test execution: auth tokens, feature flags, cached data.
- [How to Assert Clipboard in Kane CLI](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-checkpoint-devtools-clipboard.md): Verify what a Copy button actually copied, extract copied values into variables, and confirm clipboard state, using an isolated test clipboard.
- [How to Use Kane CLI Agent Mode](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-agent-mode.md): Use the --agent flag to get structured NDJSON output from Kane CLI: designed for AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI.
- [How to Run Kane CLI Tests in Parallel](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-parallel-execution.md): Run multiple independent Kane CLI browser tests in parallel using shell background processes or AI agent sub-tasks.
- [How to Run Kane CLI in CI/CD](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-cicd.md): Integrate Kane CLI into GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, Bitbucket Pipelines, and Docker for automated browser testing.
- [How to Use Kane CLI in AI Coding Agents](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-skills.md): Install the Kane CLI skill for Claude Code, Codex CLI, or Gemini CLI to enable browser automation directly from your AI coding agent.
- [Kane CLI Command & Flag Reference](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-cli-reference.md): Complete command and flag reference for Kane CLI: all commands, options, exit codes, TUI slash commands, keyboard shortcuts, and directory structure.
- [Kane CLI Error & Result Codes Reference](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-error-codes.md): Complete reference of Kane CLI result codes: what each code means, why it occurred, and what action to take. Designed for both human and AI agent consumption.
- [How to Troubleshoot Kane CLI Issues](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-troubleshooting.md): Fix common Kane CLI issues: Chrome launch failures, auth errors, run timeouts, variables not resolving, upload failures, and Agent Mode output problems.
- [sharp Install Failure](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-troubleshooting-sharp.md): Why the sharp image library can fail to install with Kane CLI, the three common causes, how to fix each one, and what still works when sharp is unavailable.
- [Kane CLI Changelog & Release Notes](https://www.testmuai.com/docs/kane-cli-changelog.md): Kane CLI release history, version notes, and links to GitHub releases.
